help.name: Controls
help.desc: Every mod shortcut, for keyboard and controller.

items.name: F1
items.text: Opens and closes this accessibility settings menu.

items.name: H
items.text: Opens and closes the mapping cursor in dungeons. I, K, J and L then move it: I ahead, K behind, J left, L right.

items.name: N
items.text: While the mapping cursor is open, switches between Walk and Look mode. Otherwise, on a dungeon floor, turns the wall sound on or off.

items.name: B
items.text: Turns the camera to face north, using the game's own smooth camera turn. Works in dungeons and anywhere the camera can rotate; says so if the camera is fixed.

items.name: Shift and slash
items.text: World helper. In town, in houses and shops, and in dungeon lobbies, reads where you are standing and then describes the whole place: its layout, landmarks and exits. Walking around these maps also announces the spot you enter, such as a shop front, a doorway or an exit, and the Check prompt names what it points at.

items.name: Shift N
items.text: Switches the mapping cursor between Compass and Camera directions.

items.name: I, K, J and L
items.text: Two jobs. With the mapping cursor open they move it: I ahead, K behind, J left, L right. On big info panels, like a persona's status or an analyzed enemy, they read the panel piece by piece: I and K move between rows, J and L step through the row's values.

items.name: Period
items.text: Shadow radar on or off.

items.name: Slash
items.text: Stairs beacon on or off.

items.name: Comma
items.text: Chest beacon on or off.

items.name: P
items.text: Sound beacon toward the selected navigation target, in dungeons and in town.

items.name: Minus and Equals
items.text: Previous and next navigation category, like doors, chests, shadows, stairs or places.

items.name: Left bracket and Right bracket
items.text: Previous and next entry in the current category, nearest first, with live distances.

items.name: Backslash
items.text: Speaks the selected entry's name and distance.

items.name: Backspace
items.text: Auto walk to the selected entry. Press Backspace again to cancel the walk.

items.name: M
items.text: Speaks the area, time, date and weather.

items.name: G
items.text: Speaks your money, in the pause menu, in shops and in the Velvet Room.

items.name: O
items.text: Party HP and SP.

items.name: Shift O
items.text: In battle, the currently acting character's name and status.

items.name: U
items.text: Enemy status, in battle.

items.name: Semicolon and Quote
items.text: Cycle through your party members one at a time, reading each member's status. Works in and out of battle.

items.name: Shift F
items.text: Quick interact menu in supported rooms, to reach the TV, the fridge, your desk and more.

items.name: Shift M
items.text: Dialogue reader on or off.

items.name: Shift Comma
items.text: Cutscene subtitle reader on or off.

items.name: Shift Period
items.text: Cutscene descriptions on or off.

items.name: Shift P
items.text: Repeats the last spoken line.

items.name: Shift Left bracket and Shift Right bracket
items.text: Step back and forward through the speech history.

children.name: Controller
children.desc: All controller combos. The triggers are the mod layer: hold one or both triggers and press a button.

items.name: Both triggers and Start
items.text: Opens and closes this accessibility settings menu.

items.name: Inside the settings menu
items.text: D-pad up and down move between rows, left and right change the value, A enters, B goes back.

items.name: Both triggers and A
items.text: Shadow radar on or off.

items.name: Both triggers and B
items.text: Stairs beacon on or off.

items.name: Both triggers and X
items.text: Chest beacon on or off.

items.name: Both triggers and Y
items.text: Wall sound on or off.

items.name: Both triggers and D-pad up
items.text: Repeats the last spoken line.

items.name: Both triggers and D-pad left or right
items.text: Step back and forward through the speech history.

items.name: Both triggers and D-pad down
items.text: Dialogue reader on or off.

items.name: Both triggers and right stick click
items.text: Cutscene subtitle reader on or off.

items.name: Both triggers and left stick click
items.text: Cutscene descriptions on or off.

items.name: Right trigger and A
items.text: Party HP and SP.

items.name: Right trigger and B
items.text: Enemy status, in battle.

items.name: Right trigger and X
items.text: Speaks your money, in the pause menu, in shops and in the Velvet Room.

items.name: Right trigger and Y
items.text: Speaks the area, time, date and weather.

items.name: Right trigger and D-pad
items.text: Two jobs. Moves the mapping cursor: up ahead, down behind, left and right sideways. On big info panels, like a persona's status or an analyzed enemy, it reads the panel piece by piece: up and down move between rows, left and right step through the row's values.

items.name: Right trigger and left stick click
items.text: Mapping cursor on or off. In battle, reads the current character instead.

items.name: Right trigger and right stick click
items.text: Mapping cursor Walk or Look mode.

items.name: Right trigger and a shoulder button
items.text: Cycle through your party members one at a time, reading each member's status. Works in and out of battle.

items.name: Left trigger and D-pad left or right
items.text: Previous and next navigation category.

items.name: Left trigger and D-pad up or down
items.text: Previous and next entry in the category.

items.name: Left trigger and A
items.text: Speaks the selected entry's name and distance.

items.name: Left trigger and B
items.text: Sound beacon toward the selected target.

items.name: Left trigger and Y
items.text: Turns the camera to face north. Works wherever the camera can rotate.

items.name: Left trigger, right trigger and Back
items.text: World helper: reads where you stand and describes the place.

items.name: Left trigger and left stick click
items.text: Auto walk to the selected entry. Again to cancel.

items.name: Left trigger and X
items.text: Quick interact menu in supported rooms.

items.name: Left trigger and right stick click
items.text: Mapping cursor Compass or Camera directions.

items.name: Entering your name, new game
items.text: Each name field holds up to 8 letters, and you enter your last name first. Type it, then press E on the keyboard, or the right shoulder button on a controller, to move to the next field. Type your first name the same way. When done, press X on the keyboard, or Start on a controller, to finish. If it will not finish, you typed something the game will not accept. Press Escape to clear the field and start that name over.

items.name: Moving in dungeons
items.text: Browse targets with the bracket keys and press Backspace to auto walk there. The walker follows the map, opens doors on the way, and tells you if it has to give up. Press Backspace again any time to stop. Stairs take you to the next floor, and new areas appear in the browser as you explore.

items.name: Shadow encounters
items.text: The shadow radar, on and off with the period key, plays every shadow around you from its direction: louder means closer, a higher pitch means it is in front of you and a lower one behind you, and the pitch rises further while it sees you. A falling sweep means a shadow close by is looking at you. To ambush one, first get behind it: while the nearest shadow has its back to you, soft ticks play from its direction. Walk toward the ticks; they speed up as you get closer. If the ticks stop and a low two-note warning plays, the shadow is turning toward you, so stop or back away and wait for the ticks to come back. When you are close enough, squarely behind it and facing it, a bright double chime plays: press the confirm button right away. Walking in works better than running, and the chime only plays while the shadow is in reach. The battle then starts with You struck first. If a shadow hits you first you hear Ambushed, and a normal start says nothing. The ticks, the warning and the chime play even with the radar off, and each has its own volume in Sound volumes.

items.name: The wall sound
items.text: The wall sound hums where walls are: a different tone ahead, behind, left and right, louder as the wall gets closer, silent toward open space. Doors nearby play their own distinct sound. The wall sound starts off each game session; turn it on when you want it.

items.name: Beacons
items.text: The stairs beacon, the chest beacon and the navigation beacon each loop a sound toward their target. Closer means louder and faster ticks. When the target is behind you the sound is muffled and slightly lower. The stairs beacon needs the stairs discovered on your map first, so explore a little if it is silent.

items.name: The mapping cursor
items.text: The mapping cursor reads the dungeon map cell by cell. In Walk mode each press steps your character one tile. In Look mode you scout the map without moving, and Backspace walks to the surveyed spot. Directions can be Compass, fixed north south west east, or Camera, relative to where you face.

items.name: Reading info panels
items.text: Big information screens, like a persona's status or an analyzed enemy, are too dense to read in one breath, so the mod reads them piece by piece. Use I, K, J and L, or the right trigger with the d-pad: up and down move between rows, like stats, resistances or skills, and left and right step through the values inside a row. Explore any panel at your own pace, and repeat a piece as often as you like.

items.name: Battles
items.text: Battles read themselves: turns, menus, damage and results are spoken. Press O for party HP and SP, U for enemy status, and Q for quick analyze of the targeted enemy. Analyze reveals an enemy's weaknesses once discovered, and the skill menus speak costs and descriptions.

items.name: Town travel
items.text: In town, browse places, exits and people with the same bracket keys and auto walk with Backspace. The mod confirms arrival and tells you when the interact prompt is ready. The P beacon guides you to the selection by ear, and the quick interact menu jumps you to objects inside supported rooms.

items.name: Fishing
items.text: Fish at the river or the sea with a rod and bait. Choosing bait reads each bait with how many you own and which fish it attracts. After you cast, wait for a quick three-note chime: that is the bite, so press Action right away. Then comes the reeling gauge, played as a tone that moves left and right with the bobber; its pitch rises the farther the bobber is from the middle. In the middle, the blue area, the pulsing stops and a deep steady sound joins in, with a short tick as you enter. Hold Action only on that steady sound and let go as soon as the pulsing returns. Holding Action outside the blue strains the line: the mod says Strain 1 to Strain 4, and the fifth snaps it. Steer against the drift with left and right: a short press pushes gently, and holding pushes harder the longer you hold. A controller's left stick works the same way. At sea the blue area gets narrower while the fish struggles, so it is harder. The bite chime and the reel tone have their own volumes in Sound volumes.

items.name: Bug catching
items.text: At the shrine tree you get one swing of the net a day, except on rainy days and in the depth of winter. After the bugs gather, the round starts with a sound, and about five seconds later the mod plays one short high chime: press Action right when you hear it. The perfect moment lasts only a fifth of a second and starts just after the chime. The game's own sounds come a little later, so reacting to them is too late. If you wait too long the round starts over, so you can let one pass and swing on the next chime. A perfect swing catches four bugs, a slightly off one two, and a bad one one; reading the bug books adds more. The chime has its own volume in Sound volumes.

items.name: This guide is arranged by date.
Open only the parts you have already reached in your own game.
Names are left out on purpose, so nothing is spoiled.
Read each part on the day it happens, not before.
There is one thing you must do.
Max the Aeon social link before the end of December.
1, head to the Central Shopping District, North, and talk with Kanji's mother who is standing outside the textile shop. She tells you to ask the boy who had been around him.
2, next you need to talk with the kid who Kanji has been hanging out with. Head to Junes and speak with the lady there, who will tell you to check back tomorrow.
3, the next day, return to Junes and talk to the boy in blue to gather more information. This will give you all the info needed to find Kanji.
1, go to Practice Building second floor at school and talk to the Risette fan. This is the chubby student near the washroom and art room.
2, go to Shopping District, South, and talk to Rise's grandmother by Marukyu Tofu.
3, go to Samegawa Flood Plain and talk to the kind man.

4, the next day come back to Samegawa Flood Plain and look for the photographer. Talk to him and select trade information, then she's different than on TV, then also say you think she is stressed. This will give you all the information you need to find Rise.
1, the first step to gathering information is talking to Kanji. Head to the Samegawa Flood Plain riverbank to find him. Kanji will recommend asking Dojima about the murderer.

2, Dojima will be located in Shopping District, South. He will scold you for investigating the case on your own. More importantly, he will mention that Adachi is nowhere to be found. The next step must wait until tomorrow.

3, go to Junes to find Adachi. When prompted, say I'll tell Dojima. This will lead you to Souzai Daigaku in Shopping District, North. Ask the shopkeeper if the boy had worked for them at an earlier time. The next step must wait until tomorrow.
4, talk to the boy in front of Marukyu Tofu shop in Shopping District, South. He will show you a picture of Mitsuo Kubo. You will now be able to enter the TV at Junes and search for him.
1, go to Classroom Building first floor of Yasogami High School. Speak to the girl in front of Classroom 1-1.
2, go to Practice Building first floor of Yasogami High School. Speak to the female student near the entrance.
3, go to Shopping District, North. Talk to the police officer on Monday, Wednesday, or Friday. He will be across the street from Konishi Liquors.
4, talk to Chie at the Samegawa Flood Plain riverbank. She should appear only after talking to the last police officer.
5, return to the same police officer at Shopping District, North, and talk to him again.
6, talk to the woman near the shrine's entrance and the textile shop at Shopping District, North.
7, talk with the police officer at Shopping District, South, on a Tuesday, Thursday, or Saturday. The way in will now be available.
Note, you must follow this guide in the order it is written.
1, talk to the shopping woman at Shopping District, North.
2, ask the female student at Junes if she recalls anyone suspicious.
3, ask the female student near the bookstore at Shopping District, South, if she recalls anyone suspicious.
4, talk to everyone in town about the murders and if they've seen anyone suspicious. Eventually the team will meet up at Aiya's Chinese Restaurant. This will progress the story.
On December 3 you must choose correctly, or you will get the bad ending.
Only the answer for each choice is listed here.
On December 5 you are asked what you believe.
Choose the truth, or you will get the bad ending.
After you have greeted all of the social links you maxed, you are offered to return home and pack. Choose no.
Make your way to Junes and check the elevator.
Choose to stop by the food court one last time, and after the discussion, go on.
Then head to the riverbank at the Samegawa Flood Plain and speak with Dojima.
Then go to the Central Shopping District and enter the Velvet Room.
Then go down the street to the gas station where you first arrived in April, and speak with the attendant.
They will try to stop talking. Keep questioning them each time they cut you off.
When you are ready, head to Junes and go to the food court.
